:::{#exm-hermitian-matrix}
#### A Hermitian matrix

$$
\underbrace{\matr{A}}_{2 \times 2} =
\begin{bmatrix}
2 & 1 - i \\
1 + i & 3
\end{bmatrix}
$$

is Hermitian:
transposing swaps the off-diagonal entries,
and conjugating turns $1 + i$ back into $1 - i$ and $1 - i$ back into $1 + i$,
so $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}} = \matr{A}$.
The diagonal entries of a Hermitian matrix must be real,
because $a_{jj} = \overline{a_{jj}}$,
and only a real number is its own conjugate:
if $a + b\,i = a - b\,i$, then the imaginary parts give $b = -b$, so $b = 0$.

Every real symmetric matrix is Hermitian,
because for a real matrix $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}} = \tp{\matr{A}}$.

:::
